Incident Name: Oakridge Industrial Park Anhydrous Ammonia Release
4 MapSketch include sketch showing the t: North-oriented map of a 2.0-mile radius centered at Cold Storage Logistics Building 7, 100 Industrial Parkway, Edison, New Jersey. The primary site is rooftop Mechanical Room 3, where an 8-inch high-pressure ammonia chiller line fractured. A 400-yard plume affects the loading dock and northern Industrial Parkway. Meadowlands Residential Community 0.9 miles East and Edison Transit Center 1.2 miles Southeast are threatened. Edison Police drone DRONE-PD-1 observed dense white fog drifting East-Northeast at 5 mph. No product entered storm drains; contamination is confined to industrial ground and rooftop surfaces, with no shoreline impact. Show Staging Area Foxtrot at Edison High School, the Command Post at Edison Fire Station 4, the 1,000-foot Exclusion Zone, and Industrial Parkway traffic-control points.
5 Situation Summary and Health and Safet: At 07:45, mechanical vibration severed an 8-inch refrigeration line and released approximately 3,000 lb of anhydrous ammonia. Building 7 was evacuated of 85 employees and a 1,000-foot isolation perimeter was established. Hazards include chemical asphyxiation, pulmonary edema, permanent ocular injury, cryogenic burns, enclosed-space flammability at 15-28% LEL, and roof-deck falls. Enforce a 1,000-foot Exclusion Zone; require Level A vapor suits with SCBA for roof entry and Level B for ground backup; continuously monitor ammonia at perimeter boundaries; deploy high-volume water curtains; and operate dual-basin chemical-wash decontamination at the main entrance.
7 Current and Planned Objectives: Enforce the 1,000-foot Exclusion Zone and isolate Building 7 HVAC intake by 08:30; make Level A roof entry and isolate the receiver valve by 11:00; deploy water-curtain nozzles by 09:30; continuously monitor air along the Meadowlands border by 09:00; and establish Unified Command by 08:45.
ActionsRow1: Edison Fire Engines 4 and 6 responded and assisted with the Building 7 evacuation.
ActionsRow2: Chief E. Sullivan established Local Command and closed Industrial Parkway at Kilmer Road.
ActionsRow3: Middlesex County Hazmat Team 2 arrived and established perimeter air monitoring and water-fog curtain monitors.
ActionsRow4: NJ DEP and the EPA Region 2 OSC arrived; Unified Command was established at Station 4.
ActionsRow5: Drone reconnaissance confirmed that water curtains reduced downwind cloud density by 60%.
ActionsRow6: Entry Team 1 in Level A PPE executes emergency roof entry to isolate the main refrigeration manifold.
ActionsRow7: Begin mechanical ventilation of Building 7 through a charcoal scrubber array.
ActionsRow8: Conduct clearance air sampling inside Building 7 before facility re-entry.
